explain.say: Imagine two neighbours who speak the same language but run their homes in totally different ways. That was Athens and Sparta in ancient Greece. Each was a city-state, a city that rules itself like a small country. Look at the two sides of the board.

explain.say: Look at the Athens side. From about 508 BCE, Athenian citizens voted on laws themselves. We call this democracy, which means rule by the people. But only free men born in Athens could vote, not women, enslaved people or foreigners. Does that sound like everyone?

explain.say: Now the Sparta side. Sparta had two kings and a council of elders. From age seven, boys left home to train as soldiers. Spartan women could own land and do sport, more freedom than women in Athens had. Which city would you pick?

faq.q: What was democracy in Athens like?
faq.a: Citizens met in an assembly on a hill called the Pnyx and voted on laws by show of hands. Many officials were chosen by lottery. Only adult male citizens could take part.

faq.q: What was life like for a Spartan boy?
faq.a: At about age seven, boys left home for the agoge, a tough training school. They learned to fight, cope with hunger and obey, and served in the army until about age 60.

faq.q: Did women have more rights in Sparta or Athens?
faq.a: In Sparta. Spartan women could own and run land and did sport. In Athens, citizen women mostly stayed at home and could not vote or own much property.
asks: How were women treated in Sparta?

faq.a: In 480 BCE a small Greek force led by King Leonidas of Sparta held a narrow pass against a huge Persian army for three days. The Greeks lost, but their stand became famous.

faq.q: Why did Athens and Sparta go to war?
faq.a: Both wanted to lead Greece. Athens grew rich and powerful from its navy and allies, and Sparta feared it. The Peloponnesian War lasted from 431 to 404 BCE.

facts: Athenian democracy began with the reforms of Cleisthenes around 508 BCE.
The Peloponnesian War between Athens and Sparta lasted from 431 to 404 BCE.

quiz.say: Who could vote in ancient Athens?
quiz.why: Only free adult men born to Athenian families could vote.

wrong.1: Women, enslaved people and foreigners could not vote.
wrong.2: Athens had no king; citizens voted themselves.

quiz.say: What did Spartan boys do from about age seven?
quiz.why: Spartan boys entered tough military training called the agoge.

wrong.1: Athens was more famous for plays and poetry.
wrong.2: Athens had the famous navy; Sparta's strength was its army.
